diwan._note: SOURCE vulos (first-party). PER-ARCHITECTURE: pins BOTH linux binaries from the vul-os/diwan v0.1.0 release via `artifacts`, so an arm64 box installs the arm64 build instead of being told the OS's own office suite is unavailable. CHECKSUM EVIDENCE 2026-08-16: each asset was downloaded fresh and sha256'd locally, and each digest equals BOTH the line for it in the release's own checksums.txt AND the digest GitHub publishes for the asset - three independent statements per artefact (amd64 467f27fc..., arm64 2e92fc07...). BOOT EVIDENCE: installed by the product's own appnet.InstallFromRegistry and launched exactly as this recipe specifies, in a debian:trixie-slim container on linux/amd64 AND linux/arm64; `file` confirmed the per-arch binary really is x86-64 resp. ARM aarch64, GET / returned the real Diwan SPA (HTTP 200, <title>Diwan</title>) and GET /api/files returned 200, with the SQLite state created under data/. BINARY_NAME: the release assets are named diwan-linux-amd64 and diwan-linux-arm64, but `command` is one string for every architecture, so binary_name pins the installed path to bin/diwan on both. PORT: diwan v0.1.0 has no port flag and no env override for server.addr, so the port is a LITERAL in data/diwan.yaml written by post_install. That is correct rather than fragile because appPort is taken verbatim from this recipe's `port` field (backend/cmd/server/main.go:1853) and is not pool-allocated - only the HOST port is - so ${PORT} at launch always equals 8080. It must be a literal because ${PORT} is NOT expanded during post_install (only into `command`, at launch, launcher.go:248). CHOWN: apps are exec'd as nobody (uid 65534, launcher.go:52-53) but InstallFromRegistry creates the app dir 0755 root-owned and never chowns it, so post_install hands data/ and uploads/ to the runtime uid; without that diwan cannot create its SQLite files. See roadmap/FIRST-PARTY-REGISTRY-TRUTH.md and roadmap/PER-ARCH-ARTIFACTS.md.

jellyfin._note: PARKED FOR HONEST IGNORANCE UNTIL 2026-08-17; BOTH MISSING MEASUREMENTS TAKEN, AND ONE OF THEM SAYS ENABLE AND THE OTHER SAYS NOT YET. (1) SELF-CONTAINMENT: MEASURED, and the answer is yes — the amd64 tarball (110228765 bytes) carries libcoreclr.so, libhostfxr.so, libhostpolicy.so, libclrjit.so and the whole System.*.dll set, so the .NET runtime is INSIDE the payload and the image does not need one. jellyfin-web ships in the same tarball (2331 members under jellyfin/jellyfin-web/), so the web client is not a second package either. The apphost was checked per architecture and they are genuinely different builds: amd64 is 'ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64' and arm64 is 'ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64' — not the kerf v0.1.9 shape. (2) FFMPEG: MEASURED, and the answer is no — zero members of the tarball match ffmpeg or ffprobe, and neither is in scripts/image-packages.txt. Jellyfin without ffprobe cannot analyse a library or transcode, so the recipe stays _disabled: an entry that installs and cannot do the thing the app is for is the defect class this format exists to remove. ENABLING IT IS ONE EDIT once ffmpeg is in the base image and scripts/verify-app-recipe.sh jellyfin passes. THIRD DEFECT FOUND WHILE MEASURING: the retired recipe ran `jellyfin --port ${PORT}`, and jellyfin HAS NO --port OPTION — the option names compiled into jellyfin.dll are exactly cachedir, configdir, datadir, ffmpeg, logdir, nowebclient, published-server-url, service, webdir. That gap is now closed by extractZip (archive/zip, in-process, so the gated image package set needs no `unzip`). ARCHIVE_STRIP 1 drops the leading lilmail/ directory, leaving ./lilmail and config.toml.example at the app root; binary_name is deliberately ABSENT because it applies only to single-binary downloads and validateRecipeSecurity refuses it on an archive rather than ignoring it. SECRETS: [jwt].secret and [encryption].key are REQUIRED (LoadConfig rejects a key that is not 16/24/32 bytes), so post_install mints both from /dev/urandom and REFUSES (exit 1) rather than writing weak or empty ones; no credential is baked into this registry. CACHE DIR: cache/ must exist before launch or lilmail logs `scheduled send unavailable (store open failed)` and runs degraded - observed, then fixed here. MAILBOX: lilmail hosts no mail and has no account system; the [imap]/[smtp] hosts written here are placeholders the owner edits to point at their OWN mailbox. port = 8090

CONFIG IS MANDATORY: wede v0.1.3 calls log.Fatal when it cannot find wede.config.json and rejects an empty password, so it fails loudly rather than starting half-configured. post_install mints a 32-character password from /dev/urandom and REFUSES (exit 1) if it cannot produce 32, rather than writing a weak or empty one; the owner reads it from wede-password.txt and no credential is baked into this registry. PORT: arrives via `-port ${PORT}`, which the launcher DOES expand (launcher.go:248); the 9090 inside the config is the file's own self-consistent default and the flag overrides it. DEPS: git is a genuine runtime dependency - wede shells out to the git binary (backend/internal/chat/chat.go:509) - not decoration. See roadmap/FIRST-PARTY-REGISTRY-TRUTH.md.
wede.author: Vulos
wede.description: Self-hosted collaborative web IDE - real-time multi-user editing, shared terminals, git and per-workspace chat, from a single binary in your browser.
wede.name: Wede

0.1.3.post_install: mkdir -p workspace && PW="$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 32)"; if [ ${#PW} -ne 32 ]; then echo "wede post-install: could not generate a 32-character password from /dev/urandom - refusing to write a config with a weak or empty password" >&2; exit 1; fi; printf '{"password":"%s","port":"9090","host":"0.0.0.0","workspace_root":"%s"}\n' "$PW" "$APP_DIR" > wede.config.json && printf '%s\n' "$PW" > wede-password.txt && chmod 640 wede.config.json wede-password.txt && chown -R 65534:65534 wede.config.json wede-password.txt workspace

wine._note: PARKED, NOT MIGRATED, 2026-08-17. wine has no expressible vehicle left and inventing one would be worse than saying so. (1) apt is gone. (2) WineHQ publishes .deb packages and no portable per-architecture tarball, so there is no artefact to pin — an `artifacts` entry here would require a URL that does not exist. (3) org.winehq.Wine on Flathub publishes SEVEN branches (stable-21.08 … stable-25.08, wow64-24.08, wow64-25.08) and NONE is named plain `stable`, so the bare id fails under FlatpakInstall; the `//branch` suffix does resolve (proved on QGIS) but every candidate is a dated branch that ages out, and WHICH one currently resolves is a `flatpak remote-info` measurement THAT WAS NOT RUN HERE. Guessing it is exactly the fabricated-value failure this work exists to remove. Disabled rather than deleted so the measured metadata survives for whoever runs that command. arch corrected to [amd64] regardless — that defect was independent of the vehicle.
